title: Lan Xang founded
description: Fa Ngum, with a Khmer army, unites the Lao principalities into the kingdom of Lan Xang, 'a million elephants'.

title: Vietnamese invasion
description: An army of Đại Việt under Lê Thánh Tông sacks the Lao capital before being driven out.

title: Capital moved to Vientiane
description: King Setthathirath moves the court down the Mekong, further from the Burmese armies.

title: That Luang built
description: Setthathirath builds the great stupa that is now the national symbol of Laos.

title: Dutch mission reaches Vientiane
description: The merchant Gerrit van Wuysthoff, among the first Europeans to visit, describes the court of Sourigna Vongsa at the height of Lan Xang.

title: Lan Xang divided
description: After a succession dispute the kingdom splits into Luang Prabang and Vientiane, and Champasak breaks away in 1713.

title: Siam takes Vientiane
description: A Siamese army captures the city and carries off the Emerald Buddha, and the Lao kingdoms become vassals of Siam.

title: Anouvong's rebellion
description: King Anouvong's attempt to throw off Siamese rule fails, Vientiane is destroyed and much of its population is deported across the Mekong.

title: Sack of Luang Prabang
description: Chinese and Tai raiders burn the town, and the French vice-consul Auguste Pavie helps the king escape, winning him over to France.

title: Laos ceded to France
description: Siam gives up the lands east of the Mekong to France by treaty, creating the French protectorate of Laos.

title: Lao Issara declares independence
description: After the Japanese surrender a nationalist government declares independence, but the French return and drive it out in 1946.

title: Pathet Lao founded
description: Prince Souphanouvong sets up a resistance government allied with the Viet Minh, the start of the communist movement that takes power in 1975.

title: Independence from France
description: France transfers its remaining powers to the royal government by treaty.

title: Kong Le's coup
description: A paratroop captain seizes the capital calling for neutrality, and the fighting that follows makes Laos a Cold War crisis.

title: Agreement on the neutrality of Laos
description: Fourteen countries promise to respect Laotian neutrality under a coalition government, an agreement that soon breaks down.

title: American bombing begins
description: The United States begins an air campaign that drops more than two million tons of bombs on Laos in nine years.

title: Vientiane ceasefire
description: The royal government and the Pathet Lao sign a ceasefire that leads to a coalition government.

title: Lao People's Democratic Republic proclaimed
description: The king abdicates and the Pathet Lao establish a one-party communist state.

title: New Economic Mechanism
description: The ruling party's congress adopts market reforms, ending collective farming and opening the economy to private business.

title: First Friendship Bridge opens
description: The first bridge over the lower Mekong links Laos with Nong Khai in Thailand.

title: Luang Prabang made a World Heritage Site
description: UNESCO lists the old royal capital, which becomes the centre of the country's tourist trade.

title: Attapeu dam collapse
description: A dam of the Xe-Pian Xe-Namnoy hydropower project fails, flooding villages and leaving thousands homeless.
